transfers.source_mechanism: Flow rate enables conduit adaptation under feedback constraints, producing optimized network topology
transfers.target_problem: A mid-sized city (population 800,000) has a traffic signal network with 247 signalized intersections. The current signal timing plan is optimized centrally every 6 months using a macroscopic traffic model, but it cannot adapt to real-time conditions: incidents, weather, special events, and construction. Re-optimizing centrally every minute is computationally infeasible and would require expensive predictive models. The city wants a distributed, adaptive signal timing approach that uses only local traffic flow measurements (vehicle count and queue length at each intersection) to adjust green-split and offset in real time, without a central optimizer.
transfers.transferred_principle: Adaptive feedback between traffic flow dynamics and signal timing parameters enables self-optimizing traffic signal networks
transfers.required_translation: Conduits → Traffic signal phases; Flow rate → Traffic volume; Conduit thickening/thinning → Green time extension/reduction; Self-repair → Signal timing adaptation; Network topology → Traffic network topology
transfers.expected_effect: Distributed adaptation of signal timing parameters (green time, offset) based on local traffic measurements without central coordination
boundary_conditions: Local measurements only (vehicle count and queue length)
failure_conditions: Failure to converge to stable timing plan
transfers.testable_prediction: Under random incident simulation (e.g., lane blockage at 10% of intersections), the adaptive signal system will reduce total network delay by at least 15% compared to the fixed 6-month optimization plan within 30 minutes of incident occurrence, while maintaining stability (no oscillations) across all 247 intersections.
